messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a 4x spike in GPU Xid errors after the driver/CUDA 535 rollout to us-east1-gpupool-2. Metrics point at NCCL watchdog resets, a few app timeouts. @aj @sourav
aj: seeing same in Prometheus, xid_rate per node jumped around 08:12UTC. alert gpu.xid_rate fired for the pool (threshold 0.02).
sourav: which Xid codes are we seeing? 31 or 45 or a mix? any kernel oops?
maria: mostly Xid 31 and 45. grabbing a short log snippet from one affected node:
```text
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] GPU0: Xid 31 - Channel exception
[2026-03-18T08:12:04Z] nv_peer2peer: timeout waiting for peer, nccl watchdog triggered
[2026-03-18T08:12:04Z] kernel: nvidia: GPU reset called for GPU0
```
olivia: do we know scope? is this isolated to that pool/region or global?
aj: quick prometheus query: `sum by(pool) (rate(gpu_xid_total[5m]))` shows the spike mostly in `us-east1-gpupool-2` and a few canary nodes. other pools flat.
maria: started pausing the next batch of driver upgrades for that cohort. tagging oncall: @oncall-bot
oncall-bot: Acknowledged. Paging oncall rotation: https://pd/redwood/integrations/xxxx
sourav: short mitigation ideas: (1) roll back driver to previous known-good (530), (2) toggle NCCL params e.g. NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0, (3) disable peer-to-peer as a test. Which is fastest?
aj: rollback is straightforward and quick; I can kick it. Also we should capture `dmesg` + `modinfo nvidia` before we reboot nodes.
maria: filing INFRA-3478 with traces & metrics. will attach repro steps.
aj: deploy-bot, please start rollback for pool us-east1-gpupool-2 to `driver-530` for the 12 nodes in the batch.
deploy-bot: Received command: `rollback --pool us-east1-gpupool-2 --to-tag driver-530 --batch 12`. Starting now; will report progress.
deploy-bot: Rollback in progress: nodes 1-12 draining, applying driver-530, restarting nvidia modules.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete for 12 nodes in us-east1-gpupool-2.
aj: post-rollback metrics: xid_rate back to baseline within ~4 minutes across the rolled-back nodes. Confirming reduction in NCCL watchdog resets.
maria: good. let's add follow-ups: create an automated pause guard in rollout pipeline + an alert runbook for these Xid/NCCL regressions.
olivia: proposal for rollout guard config (suggested):
```yaml
rollout:
  pause_on_errors: true
  error_metric: gpu_xid_rate
  threshold: 0.02
  window: 180s
  action: rollback-to-last-known-good
```
sourav: also add targeted telemetry: nccl_watchdog_count, nv_peer2peer_timeouts, and kernel module versions to the upgrade event so we can correlate.
maria: I'll add those to the INFRA ticket and draft a short runbook section: detection -> triage queries -> rollback command -> post-rollback verification.
aj: one more note: this only hit longer-context workloads (seq>2048). adding that to repro.
olivia: I'll open a PR to the rollout pipeline to add pause_on_errors and include a configurable metric name.
maria: action items summarized: 1) PR for pause guard (olivia) 2) Runbook update & INFRA-3478 doc (maria) 3) Telemetry additions & seq length tag (sourav) 4) Add alert annotation with rollback command (aj).
olivia: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
maria: closing thread for now — will link updates to INFRA-3478 and the rollout PR once merged.
